_doc: RR-EMIT reference curve spec. NOT loaded at runtime: app/domain/personas.py
globs content/personas/*.json non-recursively, so this subdirectory is
invisible to the pack loader. It is read only by backend/tools/rr_emit.py,
which emits the `unopened` nodes of the file named in `emits`.
`depths[row]` = how many classes down that row the CORE tier plays, with
rows ordered strongest-kicker-first (As = AKs, AQs, ...). Rows absent from
`depths` are not played at all; a row present with depth 0 is played by the
slope tier only (the curve's leading edge spilling into a fresh row).
`slopes[row]` overrides the slope tier widths for one row (one width per
slope tier, in tier declaration order) — the nit's curve stops one class
short in exactly five rows, and the pairs row is driven ENTIRELY by
overrides (see below).
T-M2 (2026-07-31) — the pairs row was a `tail` tier until this version.
EXPRESSIVENESS LIMIT found while adding late-position pair opens: a `tail`
row cannot carry a SEAT-VARYING band, because tier weights are global and
slope tiers skip tail-owned rows (rr_emit.emit_seat_mixes), so the only
way to give CO/BTN pair opens through a tail is to give every seat the
same ones — an over-widen the ticket forbids. Minimal resolution, no tool
change: DEMOTE the pairs row from `tail` to two slope tiers whose widths
are per-seat — `pair_open` (the late-position raise band, width 0 at every
seat but CO/BTN) above `limp_pairs` (the rest of the row, width 13 = the
whole row, which clamps to whatever is left). Slope tiers claim in
DECLARATION order, so `pair_open` must be declared first; both are
declared above `core` so the emitted mix order is unchanged at the seven
untouched seats. Consequence: every seat must now carry an explicit
`slopes.pairs`, because the `edge` tier would otherwise take a pair class
(it previously skipped the row for free as a tail row) and the row's
bottom would go unplayed. That requirement is MACHINE-CHECKED, not just
documented: `required_slopes` below makes the emitter reject a seat that
omits it (review fold, refuter I2 — a silent truncation is invisible to
the RR-LINT belt, which only sees row GAPS, never a short row bottom).
The `limp` weight 0.4 is IDENTICAL in both pair tiers on purpose: W5-b1's
verbatim-limp law. CO/BTN pair opens convert FOLD mass (0.6 -> 0.3), never
limp mass, so every pair class limps at exactly 0.4 at all nine seats.
`raise_pct` is an ASSERTED ANNOTATION, never an emitter input: the combo-
weighted raise width the emitted node actually produces, cross-checked by
test_rr_emit.py. Floors are authored; they are never fitted to a target.
There is deliberately nowhere in this file to put a percentile or width
parameter (range-representation-design.md sec.1).
